Bach: mice ate flour—if dried before Passover sift and keep after Passover; found on Passover all forbidden benefit; sack unmoved—take bite place, tie, sift all sack, may retain, forbidden eat Passover—all when mouse ate flour; bit only sack doubt ate nothing—even Passover may retain, forbidden eat, even before Passover lest chametz dried crumbles—end. I explained all this in responsum. Maharam Lublin 119 on mouse-bitten sacks sifted—pressure: take other guarded flour first two nights, bake matzot from bitten flour before Passover; sifted flour from that sieve—no stringency, all permitted—end. Taz: even water fell and dried, if recognizes moist place take and sift rest; certainly mouse bites around bite, sift rest, eat Passover—end. Mice be more stringent—wicked mice through sack, especially barrel—Geonim stringent—end:
Dew, etc. Chicken droppings do not leaven (Tur); likewise wheat in animal dung (Rokeach); appears bile also does not leaven—like blood and putrid moisture—permitted dough for healing:
Whether saliva, urine, and the like leaven. Containing 6 seifim: (1) A person shall not (1) chew (1) wheat (1) and place on (2) his wound (2) because they leaven—for (3) saliva leavens:

(2) One who gives barley to his animal and finds saliva (3) among them must burn them: {Rama: But from unspecified need not concern since already nullified (logical opinion); and some are stringent to burn all the animal's remainder even if no visible saliva on it: (Mordechai beginning chapter Elu Overin in name of Rokeach)}
(3) A sack full of flour that became moist from (6) the wall's (7) sweat (4) is permitted; (8) and some forbid:

(9) Water fell on flour (10) or the sack became moist; (5) he should take in his hand all (11) the moist place in the sack until he washes (12) all flour in the sack; (13) and if impossible to do so (6) (2) he should sift the flour (14) and the rest is permitted—but only while moist; if the moisture (15) dried, (16) sifting (17) does not help for it crumbles (18) and mixes with the rest (19) and it is forbidden to eat it (20) on Passover (21) rather he should sift and guard until after Passover (22) and if it dried on Passover (23) it is forbidden to retain it:
(7) (22) Dew leavens (23) and likewise (8) urine (9) (24) and water of the mouth, nose, eye, and ear (25) (but blood) (R' Yerucham) (26) and milk (27) and human sweat (1) (28) do not leaven (Tur):

(1) And place on wound, etc.—through chewing in mouth wheat mixes with saliva and leavens when on wound mil measure—transgress bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei; even chewed and placed before Passover remove when sixth hour eve unless spoiled unusable for dog as 442. Poskim: all this Jewish wheat; gentile wheat gentile chews and lends Jew to place on Passover—permitted if no Jewish responsibility on poultice—for gentile poultice no bal yera'eh; if gentile has no wheat Jew may buy flour for gentile, gentile chews, Jew receives as loan only. Though chametz forbidden benefit even gentile chametz as 443—here different: benefits from chametz not in manner of enjoyment—only rabbinic prohibition; illness even without danger they did not decree; nevertheless if can heal by softening wheat poultice with fruit juice—not proper through saliva:

(3) Must burn them—for saliva leavens as above—must burn; though animal did not eat mil measure—if not burn will leaven and transgress bal yera'eh:

(6) The wall—and likewise wooden wall that sweats:

Nevertheless not better than fruit juice—if fruit juice with water hastens leaven as 462—do not knead l'chatchila; if moist still sift and retain moist until after Passover; remainder knead and bake for Passover. Poskim: all this wall sweat; if sweat from heat and steam of hot blood in it as hot water tub and sack moistened thereby—for all it is water offspring and leavens:
